/-!
# Quadrisecants of wild knots

A *quadrisecant* of a curve in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is a straight line that meets the curve in
(at least) four distinct points. A *knot* is a subset of $\mathbb{R}^3$ that is the image of a
topological embedding of the circle. Following Kuperberg, a knot is *tame* if some
homeomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^3$ carries it onto a polygonal (equivalently, piecewise linear or
smooth) knot, and *wild* otherwise.

It has been conjectured that every wild knot has infinitely many quadrisecants.
Kuperberg's original conjecture is stated for wild arcs; the Wikipedia list states it for
wild knots, and this is the version formalised here.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Quadrisecant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadrisecant)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Ku94] Kuperberg, G., *Quadrisecants of knots and links*. J. Knot Theory Ramifications 3
  (1994), 41–50. [arXiv:math/9712205](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9712205)
-/

def IsPolygonalKnot (P : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  IsKnot P ∧ ∃ (n : ℕ) (v : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ³), P = ⋃ i, segment ℝ (v i) (v (i + 1))

A *polygonal knot* in `ℝ³`: a knot that is a closed polygon, i.e. the union of the closed
segments `[v i, v (i + 1)]` over a finite cyclic sequence of vertices `v`.

justification.name: QuadrisecantsOfWildKnots.IsPolygonalKnot
justification.why_needed: Needed as the target class in Kuperberg's definition of tameness (PL knots); Mathlib has no PL/polygonal curve notion.

claims.decomposer_note: Single universal Prop: for every wild knot K ⊂ ℝ³ (a topological embedding of S¹ that is not tame, i.e. not carried to a PL/smooth knot by any homeomorphism of ℝ³, per Kuperberg's definition), the set of quadrisecants (lines meeting K in at least four distinct points) is infinite; note Kuperberg's original conjecture (arXiv:math/9712205) is stated for wild arcs rather than wild knots, and the Wikipedia/statement wording 'wild knots' is the form to formalize, with 'infinitely many' meaning infinitely many distinct lines.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same universal proposition (for every topological embedding of the circle in ℝ³ that is not tame, the set of one-dimensional affine subspaces meeting the image in ≥ 4 distinct points is Set.Infinite), so the choice was about the encoding of 'tame' and style. c08 uses Kuperberg's definition literally (an ambient homeomorphism ℝ³ ≃ₜ ℝ³ carries the knot onto a closed polygon ⋃ i : Fin (n+1), segment (v i) (v (i+1)); because the image is a topological circle this is exactly a PL knot), counts distinct lines via AffineSubspace + finrank direction = 1, uses encard (so a line containing infinitely many knot points still counts, unlike ncard), avoids Fin 0/ZMod 0 pitfalls, and ships four proved API lemmas for the bespoke definitions with thorough docstrings that honestly record the wild-arc vs wild-knot discrepancy. The 'finite union of segments' variants (c03, c05, c06) and c04 are also correct; c02's explicit simple-polygon definition is correct but needlessly intricate. c01 and c07 encode tameness via Mathlib's chart-based IsSmoothEmbedding (c01 with ⊤ = ω, i.e. analytic), which is mathematically equivalent for knots but indirect and relies on heavy new manifold machinery, so the PL encoding was preferred. Edits to c08: copyright year 2026 (repo convention), short docstrings on two API lemmas.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Quadrisecants of wild knots

A *quadrisecant* of a curve in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is a straight line that meets the curve in
(at least) four distinct points. A *knot* is a subset of $\mathbb{R}^3$ that is the image of a
topological embedding of the circle. Following Kuperberg, a knot is *tame* if some
homeomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^3$ carries it onto a polygonal (equivalently, piecewise linear or
smooth) knot, and *wild* otherwise.

It has been conjectured that every wild knot has infinitely many quadrisecants.
Kuperberg's original conjecture is stated for wild arcs; the Wikipedia list states it for
wild knots, and this is the version formalised here.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Quadrisecant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadrisecant)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Ku94] Kuperberg, G., *Quadrisecants of knots and links*. J. Knot Theory Ramifications 3
  (1994), 41–50. [arXiv:math/9712205](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9712205)
-/

open Topology
open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace QuadrisecantsOfWildKnots

/-- A (topological) *knot* in `ℝ³`: a subset that is the image of a topological embedding of the
circle. -/
def IsKnot (K : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ γ : Circle → ℝ³, IsEmbedding γ ∧ Set.range γ = K

/-- A *polygonal knot* in `ℝ³`: a knot that is a closed polygon, i.e. the union of the closed
segments `[v i, v (i + 1)]` over a finite cyclic sequence of vertices `v`. -/
def IsPolygonalKnot (P : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  IsKnot P ∧ ∃ (n : ℕ) (v : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ³), P = ⋃ i, segment ℝ (v i) (v (i + 1))

/-- A knot `K ⊆ ℝ³` is *tame* if some homeomorphism of `ℝ³` carries it onto a polygonal knot
(Kuperberg's definition, [Ku94]). -/
def IsTameKnot (K : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  IsKnot K ∧ ∃ h : ℝ³ ≃ₜ ℝ³, IsPolygonalKnot (h '' K)

/-- A knot `K ⊆ ℝ³` is *wild* if it is not tame. -/
def IsWildKnot (K : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  IsKnot K ∧ ¬ IsTameKnot K

/-- A line `ℓ` in `ℝ³` (an affine subspace with one-dimensional direction) is a *quadrisecant* of
a set `K ⊆ ℝ³` if it meets `K` in at least four distinct points. -/
def IsQuadrisecant (K : Set ℝ³) (ℓ : AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ³) : Prop :=
  Module.finrank ℝ ℓ.direction = 1 ∧ 4 ≤ (K ∩ ℓ).encard

/-- A tame knot is a knot. -/
@[category API, AMS 51 57]
lemma IsTameKnot.isKnot {K : Set ℝ³} (hK : IsTameKnot K) : IsKnot K :=
  hK.1

/-- A wild knot is a knot. -/
@[category API, AMS 51 57]
lemma IsWildKnot.isKnot {K : Set ℝ³} (hK : IsWildKnot K) : IsKnot K :=
  hK.1

/-- A polygonal knot is tame (take the identity homeomorphism). -/
@[category API, AMS 51 57]
lemma IsPolygonalKnot.isTameKnot {P : Set ℝ³} (hP : IsPolygonalKnot P) : IsTameKnot P :=
  ⟨hP.1, Homeomorph.refl ℝ³, by simpa using hP⟩

/-- A knot is either tame or wild, and not both. -/
@[category API, AMS 51 57]
lemma isTameKnot_xor_isWildKnot {K : Set ℝ³} (hK : IsKnot K) :
    Xor' (IsTameKnot K) (IsWildKnot K) := by
  by_cases h : IsTameKnot K
  · exact Or.inl ⟨h, fun h' => h'.2 h⟩
  · exact Or.inr ⟨⟨hK, h⟩, h⟩

/--
**Quadrisecants of wild knots.**
Every wild knot $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ (a topological embedding of the circle that is not
carried to a polygonal knot by any homeomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^3$) has infinitely many
quadrisecants, i.e. infinitely many distinct straight lines each meeting $K$ in at least four
distinct points.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51 57]
theorem quadrisecants_of_wild_knots (K : Set ℝ³) (hK : IsWildKnot K) :
    {ℓ : AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ³ | IsQuadrisecant K ℓ}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end QuadrisecantsOfWildKnots

items: Knot = subset of ℝ³ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3), via the repo's scoped `ℝ³` notation) equal to the range of a topological embedding `Circle → ℝ³`, following the idiom of Wikipedia/InscribedSquare.lean.

Tame = Kuperberg's definition (arXiv:math/9712205, Def. in §'Arbitrary tame knots and links'): there exists a homeomorphism h : ℝ³ ≃ₜ ℝ³ with h '' K a polygonal knot. Of Kuperberg's three equivalent targets (polynomial / PL / smooth) the PL one was chosen because it is elementary to state faithfully; a 'smooth knot' would require an immersion condition to avoid subtle wild-image issues.

Polygonal knot = a knot that equals ⋃ i : Fin (n+1), segment ℝ (v i) (v (i+1)) for a finite cyclic vertex sequence. Indexing over `Fin (n+1)` (never `ZMod 0 = ℤ`) is essential: an infinite polygonal union could be a wild knot (e.g. Fox–Artin style examples). Since h '' K is automatically a topological circle, requiring only that it be a finite union of segments is equivalent to being a PL knot; the `IsKnot` conjunct in `IsPolygonalKnot` is redundant inside `IsTameKnot` but keeps the definition correct standalone.

Wild = knot that is not tame (IsKnot K ∧ ¬ IsTameKnot K), per the decomposition notes; Kuperberg's original conjecture concerns wild arcs, but the Wikipedia 'wild knots' wording is what was formalized as instructed.

Quadrisecant = an affine subspace ℓ with `Module.finrank ℝ ℓ.direction = 1` (a line) such that `4 ≤ (K ∩ ℓ).encard`, i.e. at least four distinct intersection points (as in the decomposition notes and Kuperberg's 'secant with two middle points'). A line containing a segment of K therefore counts as a quadrisecant (encard = ⊤ ≥ 4); this matches the 'at least four' reading. 'Exactly four' was deliberately not used.
'Infinitely many quadrisecants' = `Set.Infinite` of the set of such lines, lines being `AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ³` so distinct elements are distinct lines.

Not stated as answer(sorry) since the source is a declarative conjecture, not a question. AMS tags 51 (geometry) and 57 (manifolds/knot theory). Four small proven `category API` lemmas were added as basic tests of the bespoke definitions, per CONTRIBUTING.md.

reviewer_notes: Source ambiguity: Kuperberg (arXiv:math/9712205, final section) conjectures 'every wild arc in ℝ³ has infinitely many quadrisecants', while the Wikipedia list entry (the statement being formalized) says 'wild knots'; per the decomposition table the knot form is formalized and the discrepancy is recorded in the module docstring. Kuperberg's own definition of a quadrisecant is a secant segment with two middle points (a 4-point configuration) rather than a line; the table's reading (distinct lines with ≥ 4 distinct points of K) is used, which is the stronger 'infinitely many' claim and matches Wikipedia's definition. Tameness follows Kuperberg's definition (homeomorphism of ℝ³, not S³, onto a PL knot); the PL, smooth and polynomial variants are classically equivalent. Boundary checks: IsWildKnot is satisfiable (Fox–Artin knots), finrank direction = 1 excludes ⊥/points/planes, encard ≥ 4 handles infinite intersections, Fin (n+1) indexing avoids the empty cyclic index type.
